channel.project_pack_ref: Clinic Retail Corner and Supply Shelf Optimisation

threads.thread_goal: Align on project scope, roles, and initial mapping of current shelves

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the channel for the Clinic Shelf Optimisation project. The main goal is to create a standard, safer, and more efficient layout for our retail and medical supply shelves. First step is to map out what we currently have. I've started a doc for this in A1. Can everyone take a look at T1 and share any immediate pain points you see daily? Let's get a clear picture of the 'before' state.

Great to get this started. My biggest issue is the mixed-up allergy meds and vitamins in the retail section. Customers are always asking for help. I can start adding photos of the current layout to A1 this afternoon.

Thanks for kicking this off. For the medical supplies, the bandages and sterile dressings are often in different places depending on who did the last restock. It causes delays when we're with a patient. We should define a permanent home for them.
Excellent point. That's exactly the kind of thing we need to fix. Let's make sure that's captured in the pain points section of A1.
ok sounds good. which shelves are we doing? all of them?

Good question. The scope includes all patient-facing retail shelves in the main waiting area and the three medical supply shelf units in the clinical prep room. The backroom storage is out of scope for now. Let's make that official.
I can help with the mapping. When do you need it by?
I've already started on the retail side. Maybe you can focus on the medical supply shelves? I think we can get it all done by EOD tomorrow if we split it.
That's a great plan. So to confirm, @515752 will own updating the layout map A1, with help from @211931, and the deadline for the complete 'before' map is EOD tomorrow. That works.
ok i can do that

threads.thread_goal: Agree on the new standard shelf layout and zoning

messages.text: Hi all, the first draft of the new layout is ready for review in A1. I've created two tabs: one for retail and one for medical supplies. Let me know your thoughts.

Thanks @515752, this is a fantastic start. Looking at the medical supply layout, we need to ensure we're meeting all clinical requirements per T7. I've added some notes to A8 about temperature-sensitive items and high-risk medication storage. Specifically, the refrigerated items need to be on a dedicated shelf, not mixed with other supplies. Can we adjust the map to reflect that?

The retail layout looks much better. Grouping the baby products together is a good idea. One question: should the high-demand pain relief be closer to the counter for easier access and to keep an eye on it?

Good catch, @446674. I'll update the medical layout now to create a separate 'Refrigerated Zone'. For the retail side, @362964, yes, we can move the pain relief to the first aisle. I'll make that change too.
where are the gloves going?
They are in the 'PPE & Disposables' zone on the medical supply map in A1, right next to the masks and aprons for quick access.
Okay, A1 is updated with those changes. Let me know if this looks better.

Perfect. The retail layout with pain relief moved is approved from my side. The medical layout now correctly separates refrigerated items and groups PPE logically. I'm happy to sign off on this from a clinical perspective. With these changes, I think we can approve both layouts.
Looks good to me too. Much more logical.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise rotation, expiry, and inspection procedures

messages.text: Team, now that the layout is set, let's define the processes to maintain it. I've drafted the stock rotation procedure in A2 and the daily/weekly inspection checklist in A4. Please review and provide feedback, especially on the frequency of checks. This covers T3 and T5.
Docs look clear. For A2, I think daily expiry checks on refrigerated medical items is right, but for retail items like vitamins, maybe a weekly check is enough? Daily seems like a lot for those.

That's a fair point. We need to be rigorous but also realistic. Let's propose this: Daily expiry checks for all refrigerated and high-risk medical items. Weekly checks for shelf-stable medical supplies and all retail products. How does that sound to everyone?
That sounds much more manageable and still safe. I agree with that frequency. The checklist in A4 looks straightforward. Who is responsible for signing it off each day?
The idea is that the person doing the morning restock completes the daily checklist, and the weekend opening staff completes the weekly one. I'll add a line in A4 for initials. Any objections?
The frequency split works for me.
so we just write our name on the paper?

Exactly. Just your initials and the date, so we know it's been done. Hearing no objections, I'll update A2 with the agreed frequencies. And with the clarification on sign-offs, let's consider the checklist A4 approved.

threads.thread_goal: Align labelling, pricing, and training approach before relayout

messages.text: Okay team, final prep before the physical relayout. I need your eyes on two documents. First is the labelling and pricing guide A3, which is critical for T4 to avoid billing errors. Second is the draft quick-reference training guide A5 for T8. We need to get this right so the rollout is smooth.

The labelling guide A3 looks good. Clear format. I've already cross-checked the top 10 retail items with the current billing system and they match. The training guide A5 is nice and visual. For the training huddles (T9), are we doing one per shift?

Great proactive check, @515752! Yes, the plan for T9 is a 15-minute huddle at the start of the morning and evening shifts next Monday and Tuesday to catch everyone. I'll book those in. Does that work?
The guides look easy to follow. I think the training schedule sounds right, it should cover all of us.
who prints the new labels?

I will handle getting the initial set of new labels printed once we approve the guide. After that, the process for printing new or updated ones is in A3. Since everyone seems happy with the guide and the training plan, let's lock these in.
Yep, training dates work for me.

threads.thread_goal: Monitor rollout, capture issues, and agree on follow-up improvements

messages.text: Morning all! The physical relayout (T6) is complete. As you work today, please log any issues—stockouts, misplaced items, confusion—in the new issue log A6. This is for T10. Also, keep an eye on patient flow around the new retail layout (T12). Let's capture feedback while it's fresh.

Looks great! I already had a patient comment on how much easier it is to find the children's medicine. I've added a note to A6 about us running low on antiseptic wipes, which became obvious with the new layout. Good catch.
I used the new inspection checklist A4 this morning, it worked well. Took about 5 minutes. Everything was in its place.
a patient asked me where the water bottles went. i showed them.
Thanks for flagging that. We might need a small temporary sign for a week or so. I'll add that to our list of potential tweaks for the post-rollout review (T11).
ok i will log things in A6.

Thanks everyone for the quick feedback. It sounds like the rollout has been smooth overall. Based on the positive comments, it seems the scope we defined was correct and covered the main problem areas. Let's formally confirm that the project scope has been successfully addressed.
Agreed, the scope felt right. The checklist from A4 is also working well, as @362964 said. It's much faster than the old way of just 'looking around'.

Excellent. Then we can also confirm the daily and weekly inspection checklist is approved for permanent use. I'll collect all this feedback for the final report A7 at the end of the week. Keep the logs in A6 coming!
